title: Revenue Leakage
description: Everything about finding, measuring, and fixing revenue leakage — definitions, examples, detection methods, and recovery playbooks.

faq.a: Revenue leakage is money your business should earn but does not — because of gaps in acquisition, conversion, retention, billing, or expansion — not because demand disappeared.

faq.q: How much revenue do businesses typically leak?
faq.a: Estimates vary by model; many B2B and subscription businesses see single-digit percentages of revenue at risk from billing errors, churn, and funnel gaps. Directional diagnostics help prioritize fixes.

faq.q: Is revenue leakage the same as churn?
faq.a: No. Churn is one source. Leakage also includes failed payments, slow follow-up, cart abandonment, unbilled usage, and missing upsells — often before a customer ever leaves.

intro: Revenue leakage is the gap between what your funnel could produce and what you actually collect. This cluster covers definitions, real-world examples, and how to detect leaks before they compound.
